reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses the magnetocaloric effect and suggests Cu as a cost-reducing structural additive in high-entropy alloys, but provides no specific prior evidence for Cu's effect on grain boundary cohesion, mechanical properties, or magnetocaloric retention in MnNiSi-based alloys. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Cu addition improves grain boundary cohesion and microstructure uniformity in alloys
Non-magnetic Cu addition does not significantly disrupt the magneto-structural transition in MnNiSi
Low-level Cu addition (3-5 at%) enhances mechanical properties (toughness, ductility)
Magnetocaloric effect (magnetic entropy change) is largely retained with low-level Cu addition
